chunks: Among them is what Al-Husayn ibn Ubaydullah informed me about, from Abu Abdillah Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Sufyan Al-Bazufari (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: The Shaykh Abu al-Qasim Al-Husayn ibn Rauh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me, saying: Our companions differed regarding al-tafwid (delegation of authority) and other matters, so I went to Abu Tahir ibn Bilal during the days of his correctness/orthodoxy and informed him of the difference of opinion. He said: Delay for me. So I delayed for him for some days, then I returned to him and he brought out for me a hadith with its chain leading to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

He said: When Allah wills a matter, He presents it to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and then to all the Imams, one after another, until it reaches the Master of the Age (peace be upon him), and then it is revealed to the world. And when the angels wish to raise a deed to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, it is presented to the Master of the Age (peace be upon him), then it goes out one after another until it is presented to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then it is presented to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So whatever descends from Allah is through their hands, and whatever ascends to Allah is through their hands, and they are never devoid of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for the blink of an eye.

key_terms.صاحب الزمان: Sahib al-Zaman (The Master of the Age, referring to the 12th Imam)
key_terms.طرفة عين: Tarfat al-'ayn (The blink of an eye)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia theological concept of Tafwid and how do the Imams function as intermediaries for divine decrees and human deeds?
ai.summary: This hadith, cited by Shaykh al-Tusi to resolve the scholarly debate on *al-tafwid* (divine delegation), illustrates the Imams as the exclusive spiritual conduits for both descending revelation and ascending human deeds. It establishes a continuous chain of authority from Allah to the Master of the Age (al-Mahdi) and back, affirming their indispensable role in cosmic governance. This narrative underscores the Shia doctrine that the Imams are never absent from the divine plan, serving as the vital link between the Creator and creation.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 351 - Narrated to me Husain bin Ubaidullah from Abu Abdullah Husain bin Ali bin Sufyan Bazufari that he said: Narrated to me Shaykh Abul Qasim Husain bin Rauh that: Our scholars had differences especially with regard to the matter of predestination etc. Before Abu Tahir Bilal became deviated, I went to him once and conveyed to him information about the differences. He said: Give me sometime. I gave him sometimes and after that I visited him again. He showed me a tradition from Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) that the Imam had said:

Whenever Allah, the Mighty and the High decides a matter, it is transferred to the Messenger of Allah (s) and after him it is transferred to Amirul Momineen (a.s) and after him to every Imam one after another till it reaches upto the Master of the age (a.s) and after that it is revealed to the world. And when angels want to take an issue to the presence of Almighty Allah; first they entrust it to the Master of the Age (a.s) and then it is presented to each in succession till it reaches the Messenger of Allah (s) who presents it to Almighty Allah. On the basis of this all that is issued from Almighty Allah is issued through the Holy Imams (a.s) and all the deeds that go upto Almighty Allah go up through the Holy Imams (a.s) and the Messenger of Allah (s) and his Ahle Bayt (a.s) are not at all even for the blink of an eye needless of Allah, the Mighty and the High. [On the contrary, they are mediums of divine grace for the people by the permission of Allah].
